tia: FYI ran reranker-cascade-v1 through the bringup matrix. metrics odd: NDCG@10 improves +2.4% but MRR@5 drops -3.8%. biggest regression on short-snippet queries (<=40 chars).
owen: did you change priming length or snippet truncation?
tia: we landed prefix-cache optimization in retrieval that trims snippets to 64 tokens for storage. offline eval used 128-token snippets. I didn't realize staging had the new trimmed artifact.
harry: trimming could change priming context and tokenization boundaries. quantized models (int8 PTQ and int4 AQT) compress logits -> small top-k gaps disappear and result in top-1 flips. did you compare fp32 vs quant with the same snippet length?
tia: ran quick parity:
- fp32 (128 snippet): ndcg +1.5 mrr -0.4
- int8 (128 snippet): ndcg +1.7 mrr -0.9
- int8 (64 snippet): ndcg +2.4 mrr -3.8
so truncation seems to amplify MRR drop under quant.
owen: can you paste the eval command and the snippet config?
tia: ```
./eval_rerank --gold holdout_snip.json --pred preds_cascade_v1.json \--metrics ndcg@10,mrr@5 \--slices short_snippet,core \--snippet-max-tokens 64 \--tokenizer spm_v5 \--model-config rerank-cascade-v1.json
```
harry: interesting. another angle: prefix-cache may also change KV cache alignment during serving; quantized kernels handle KV differently and small shift in cache offsets could change incremental decoding or scoring ordering for short contexts. any failing qids?
tia: uploaded failing_examples.jsonl and token_diffs.csv to s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/rerank/cascade/v1/1795012345/. sample qid Q-27 shows fp32 top1=D10, int8-64top1=D3; tokenized priming differs after truncation: fp32 prompt tokens length 96, truncated prompt 58 -> different boundary tokens.
owen: two mitigations: 1) enforce snippet-max-tokens parity between offline eval artifact and staging snapshot (checksum assert), 2) add a short-snippet quant smoke in CI (200 qids) that compares MRR vs fp32 and fails if drop >2.5%, 3) consider adding a tiny deterministic bias by doc_id hash to stabilize quant ties, 4) in prefix-cache patch revert KV packing change that alters offsets (if reproduces).
harry: also recommend adding a test in the eval harness that reports token-boundary divergence stats between offline-gold and staging-prompts (e.g., fraction of qids with token id diffs > 5). would catch truncation/concat issues quickly.
tia: I prototyped a small reproduce script reproduce_trunc.sh in the PR that fetches both 64/128 artifacts and runs the 250-q smoke. linking in PR.
tia: PRs I'll open: (A) onboarding checklist update to require snippet_max_tokens and prefix-cache checksum, (B) CI smoke job for short-snippet int8 parity, (C) revert candidate packing in prefix-cache for canary while we confirm. artifacts uploaded.
ci-bot: staging snapshot created: rerank-cascade-v1-trunc-check-2026-04-04T12:55:10Z :white_check_mark:
owen: please add a clear note to the model card: "quantization sensitivity: snippet truncation and KV-cache offset changes can amplify top-1 instability for short snippets". also tag infra for prefix-cache offset audit.
harry: one more thought  add a tiny soft margin in scorer: score += (doc_id_hash % 10000) * 1e-7 pre-softmax. stabilizes ties without changing fp32 ordering. we can A/B it.
tia: will include that in the tie-breaker experiment PR. thanks for the rapid triage. resolving until PRs land.
